name: Uhami
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Elugbe 1989 (subclassification comment); no grammar or phonology of Uhami located online.

new_statements.quote: Two levels of tone are clearly distinctive in Uhami: high and low. High contrasts with low in the following minimal pair: /akɔ/ [_ _] 'tooth, teeth' (LL) /ákɔ/ [- _] 'day' (HL). A third level occurs in Uhami but it is not clear whether this third level should be analysed as a third significant (mid) tone or as a downstep. The latter analysis is tentatively adopted here [...] [fn. 1:] My informants were very inconsistent with tone and this analysis must be taken as very tentative. (1973: 275) || Within the scope of the limited data at my disposal, high and low tones were found to be distinctive. A third mid level was also identified but it will probably be analysed as a downstep. (1989: 97)

The latter analysis is tentatively adopted here for two reasons:...'; footnote 1: 'My informants were very inconsistent with tone and this ana…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Uhami is described as a tone language with two distinctive levels, high and low, plus a tentatively analysed downstep (third level); both descriptions are explicitly based on limited, inconsistent data. Neither source mentions stress or accent anywhere, so no rule for stress placement can be stated. A newer, login-walled study (Tunde 2024) claims four tones (H, M, L, falling) per its abstract, again with no mention of stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone only: a third (mid) level appears in the Yoruba loan /ɔ́dɛ̄/ 'hunter' and in downstep sequences; a LMH sequence [ù dɔ̄ dé] 'you bought a house' is discussed as inconclusive evidence for a mid tone (1973: 275-276).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements concern lexical items (nouns, verbs) and short verb phrases; the completive phrase was left undescribed because of informant inconsistency (1973: 275 fn. 1). Stems are mostly monosyllabic (1989: 97).
new_statements.identity_note: Sources describe Uhami as spoken in the two Ishuas (Isua-Akoko), Oyara and probably Shosan, Ondo State (Elugbe 1989: 7; informant P. A. Longe); Tunde 2024/2025 use the endonym Ùhànmì for the same Isua-Akoko speech form (Glottolog language_note 'Ùhànmì = Uhami [uha]'). No dialect split is described; all statements refer to uham1238 itself.

sources.note: Sections: syllable structure (CV, V), consonants, consonant contrasts, 7 vowels, no vowel harmony, Tone (pp. 275-276): 'Two levels of tone are clearly distinctive in Uhami: high and low'; a third level tentatively analysed as downstep; fn. 1: informants 'very inconsistent with tone and this analysis must be taken as very tentative'. General Tone p. 90 puts Uhami in group (c) 'two tones plus downstep'. Stress/accent never mentioned.

sources.note: Morphology paper (six nominalizing strategies; data from four Isua-Akoko speakers aged 50-70). 'stress'/'accent': 0 occurrences; 'tone' only in the Edo literature review and references. Silent on Uhami prosody.
